Subject: Sudden latency spike affecting inference for patient-triage endpoint

Hi Priyom —

We're seeing a surge in p99 latency on the patient-triage endpoint starting ~08:45 PST; requests are timing out intermittently and the clinical workflow is degraded (retry storms). This correlates with higher token lengths over the last hour but we also see some 503s coming back. Can you confirm if this is on Redwood's side or something in our config?

We are on Redwood hosted inference (model: rv-13B-quant) in us-west. Attaching quick logs from our side (excerpted). Please escalate — we have active clinical trials running this morning.

Thanks,
Samir Patel

Subject: Re: Sudden latency spike affecting inference for patient-triage endpoint

Samir / Olivia —

Quick update from Redwood: thank you for the alert and the logs. We're treating this as a SEV-1 impact on production inference for your patient-triage route. Immediate actions underway: 

- Detection: our monitoring shows p99 increased from ~220ms to 2.1s beginning 08:43 PST coincident with a higher tail token distribution. No fleet-wide outage detected.
- Mitigation: we have injected additional capacity into the us-west pool for your tenant and are routing new requests to a stable model variant (rv-13B-std) to reduce decode overhead. This should improve p99 within the next 10-15 minutes.
- Investigation: engineering is collecting KV-cache metrics and tracing the long-attention path; we are also verifying recent quantization flags that were promoted earlier this week.

Immediate customer ask to you: please hold non-critical jobs and avoid large-batch replays while we stabilize.

ETA: we expect measurable p99 improvement within 15 minutes and will send another update with concrete numbers and any follow-up mitigations. If stability does not improve by 10:00 PST we will escalate to a cross-functional bridge including infra and runtime kernel owners.

We apologize for the disruption to your clinical workflows — keeping this brief while we stabilize. I will send an executive summary for your leadership shortly.

Best,
Priyom Das
Account Lead, Redwood Inference

From: aditya_rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Patel <samir@heliomed.health>, Olivia Chen <olivia.chen@heliomed.health>, priyom_das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
Cc: lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 12 Nov 2026 17:22:00 -08:00
Subject: Follow-up: remediation actions taken and next steps (runbook & short-term patch)

Samir / Olivia / Priyom —

Final update for today (post stabilization): thank you for the patience. Sequence of what we did and commitments: 

1) Stabilization timeline
- 08:43 PST: p99 spike detected.
- 08:55 PST: traffic routed to rv-13B-std variant and us-west pool scaled +20% for HelioMed tenant.
- 09:10 PST: p99 improved to sub-400ms; error rates returned to baseline.

2) Root cause (preliminary)
- A quantization flag promoted in last week's deployment caused a decode slow path on the rv-13B-quant variant under certain long-token sequences. The issue surfaced with HelioMed's distribution of long prompts.

3) Actions taken now
- Rolled back the quantization promotion for the rv-13B-quant image used by HelioMed; created a canary policy to prevent fleet-wide automatic promotion until validation completes.
- Hot patch in serving runtime to bypass a slow attention kernel for affected trace patterns (see attached runbook_patch_20261112.md).
- Added a tenant-scoped autoscale threshold to trigger earlier when tail latency increases (protects against retry storms).

4) Customer commitments and next steps
- Short term: monitor for 48 hours with increased telemetry retention for your tenant; we will provide hourly digests for the first 6 hours.
- Medium term (2-4 weeks): full postmortem with quantitative impact, regression test added to our eval harness, and targeted kernel optimization roadmap.
- We will provide a validated config for rv-13B-quant (with conservative quant flags) and a migration timetable.

Attachments: runbook_patch_20261112.md (markdown, 8KB) — contains the hot patch steps and rollback commands; latency_summary_20261112.png — p95/p99 charts; support_log_snippet.txt — excerpt you shared.

If you'd like, we can set a 30-minute bridge to review the runbook and schedule the medium-term rollout window.

Apologies again — we'll follow up with the full postmortem once the investigation completes.

Regards,
Aditya Rao
Senior Runtime Engineer, Redwood Inference
